fresh_findings.title: The set supports judging pose, not animation - and the fix is a MediaWiki API, not a video host
fresh_findings.rank: most important finding in this document
fresh_findings.argument: 449 media files, zero temporal. video/ is an empty directory. RI-WPN01-04 are windup silhouette, arc type, follow-through, recovery posture - three of the four are defined by what happens between frames. RI-AI02's bar is 'which attack is coming AND ROUGHLY WHEN' - a duration a still cannot contain. A5 rule 3 says in terms that video is first-class here and a still cannot show a windup; the axis was built entirely of stills. The project concluded IMPOSSIBLE because YouTube is closed and archive.org's holdings are too large. Both premises true, conclusion wrong: the artifact that serves these items is not a longplay, it is a per-move animation, and two wikis publish libraries of them.
verified_today: darksouls.fandom.com/api.php list=categorymembers Category:Dark Souls: Boss Attack Animations -> HTTP 200, 12 files named per move (Artorias - Heavy Slam, Somersault Attack, Overwhelming Leap, ...). R1 found this; the builder did not act on it and 15.6 does not list it as attempted or blocked.

Includes ER Moveset Neutral/Strong/War Cry/Barbaric Roar Attack Chain Longsword (= RI-WPN01-04 for one named weapon class, four times), 11 ER Skill Quickstep clips (locomotion+dodge library), Bloodstain rogier.gif (RI-JRN06), 5 enemy Ash-of-War clips (RI-AI02).

Absolute frame-exact (16.7 ms) calibration stays IMPOSSIBLE and I am not asking for it.

fresh_findings.title: block_score is confounded with scene darkness; the 'Steam re-encodes user uploads' diagnosis is refuted by the builder's own computed fields
evidence: jpeg_quality_est median = 100.0 in EVERY Steam-sourced folder including the ones called heavily recompressed; bytes_per_pixel 1.29-2.31. My own q=95 re-encode of a corpus image produced 0.31 bytes/pixel. A file at 1.3 bpp with a q~100 quantisation table is not a heavy re-encode.

make-manifest.py line 138: return (aligned/n_aligned)/(other/n_other) - the denominator IS the scene's own detail, so a dark smooth scene inflates the ratio for a fixed amount of blocking. The metric measures visibility of blocking relative to content, not information destroyed.

CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT on run-w3nextgen-t0007.jpg (corpus's cleanest, block_score 0.987), one encoder, CONSTANT q=95, only luminance varied: lum 161.9 -> 1.093 PASS; lum 80.7 -> 1.203; lum 48.1 -> 1.313; lum 28.6 -> 1.447 FAIL. The luminance effect (+0.35) exceeds the whole margin between the 1.15 threshold and interior_darkemissive's 1.29 median.

CORPUS-WIDE, one host one encoder, n=106 Steam-sourced modern files: Pearson r(mean luminance, block_score) = -0.369; r(bytes_per_pixel, block_score) = -0.588. By luminance quintile, median block_score 1.284 / 1.246 / 1.162 / 1.133 / 1.133 and fail-rate 67% down to 38%. Monotone.

A genuinely lossless dark image passes easily: deadendthrills.com serves PNG at 2560x1440 and 3840x2160; battle.png at mean luminance 47.5 (squarely in the failing quintile) scores block_score 0.998; three other DET PNGs score 0.991-0.996.
fresh_findings.correct_statement: The metric is not broken - a lossless dark frame correctly scores 1.00. What is broken is applying ONE absolute threshold to all profiles when relative encode damage is inherently larger in dark scenes at any fixed quality. interior_darkemissive, the profile defined by darkness, is held to a strictly harder standard than exterior_daylight for identical source quality. That is a permanent self-inflicted fail of exactly the kind A3's IMPOSSIBLE class exists to stop.
fresh_findings.recommended_fix: (a) exposure-relative threshold, zero downloads - the luminance-quintile table above IS the calibration; threshold at quintile median + 0.10 takes interior_darkemissive from 3 countable to ~14 and exterior_lowlight from 8 to ~18. Or gate dark profiles on jpeg_quality_est + bytes_per_pixel, which are exposure-independent and already computed. (b) lossless source only for material_closeup, where a posed surface study costs nothing - deadendthrills is art-directed photo mode and must never be the bulk of a profile.

fresh_findings.title: has_hud is a folder constant, so RI-UIX01's population is ~10 frames not 93 - and nothing in the set shows a lock-on reticle or a status-buildup bar
fresh_findings.argument: has_hud is true for 93/93 souls, 33/33 REF-A12b, 5/5 anti-generic; it varies per file in modern/ and REF-A1-A19, so this is a value typed once per folder this round. Measured: counting strongly-saturated pixels in the DS3 HP/stamina bar region, 29 of 93 souls frames return exactly 0.0000. One I opened by eye (souls-behaviour/telegraph/SB-TEL__ds3-3620431452.jpg) is a clean HUD-free photo-mode portrait of a robed scythe-bearer; its record says has_hud true and describes it as 'Dancer of the Boreal Valley standing with blades trailing before an attack'. It has no HUD and no attack. Consequences: A1 clause 3 makes the metrics battery mask a border band wherever has_hud is true, discarding real image data from 29 frames; and RI-UIX01's real population is ~10, not 93. Within those, reading all 93 depicts strings, NOT ONE names a lock-on reticle and NOT ONE names a status-buildup bar - both named explicitly by RI-UIX01, and both only appear under a specific condition, which is why a generic combat-screenshot search will never surface them.
fresh_findings.detector: fraction of pixels with max(RGB)-min(RGB) > 55 and max > 70 in box (0.03w,0.03h)-(0.35w,0.13h); < 0.012 means no DS3 HUD

fresh_findings.title: The behavioural axis is 91 of 93 one game, and A5 rule 5 asked for two
fresh_findings.argument: souls-behaviour is DARK SOULS III 91, Dark Souls Remastered 2, Elden Ring 0. A5 rule 5 ('both games count') was an invitation to breadth read as permission for depth in one title. Elden Ring's camera is not DS3's - different default FOV, different lock-on distances, a mounted mode, much larger arenas. RI-CAM01's pivot height and shoulder offset and RI-CAM03's lock-on containment law are being measured off one game's camera and generalised to 'Souls'. That is the single-source problem section 3's min-distinct-games rule exists to prevent, on the one axis where that rule was not written down. Not a source problem: Elden Ring is abundant in this repository; the souls harvest ran against 374320 and 570940 and not 1245620.

fresh_findings.title: The interval run is 56% of exterior_daylight and is the negative anchor's location; section 3's anti-curation rule and its distinct-locations rule are in tension
fresh_findings.argument: I opened two of the 24 released Witcher 3 frames: run-w3nextgen-t0007.jpg and t0305.jpg are both Novigrad half-timbered townscape, and all 24 share one identical depicts string in the catalogue. anti-generic/ holds five files with role 'NEGATIVE anchor only ... the canonical fantasy look we must not converge on', one of which is literally ANTI__w3-novigrad-half-timbered.jpg. So 56% of the mass of the profile that sets our exterior_daylight fidelity bands is one walk through the exact town another folder designates as the thing we must measure distance away from. Defensible for pure rendering-quality metrics; not for the content-sensitive bands (colour entropy, sky fraction, palette centroid, foliage statistics), where one location at 56% weight IS the band. Structurally: section 3 requires >=6 distinct locations AND >=half interval-run, and those two rules fight each other because an interval run is by construction one location.
fresh_findings.fix: computation rule, no download: any single interval-run series counts as one location and is downweighted to at most 1/locations of band mass. Then report exterior_daylight's bands computed with and without the 24 and state the delta - if small this closes for free.

fresh_findings.title: character_closeup is not short by three files; it is mostly the wrong camera
fresh_findings.argument: 13 files, of which 9 are Elden Ring cutscene or NPC portraits (Melina x2, Godrick x5, Malenia). REF-M6 is the player from behind at 40-70% of frame height, and RI-CAM07 B is explicit that the back of the head, armour, legs and hanging scabbard get more screen-time than any other surface. A cutscene close-up of Godrick answers none of that and is not even the same renderer path - cutscene cameras use different framing, LOD selection and often a different lighting rig. Wrong camera, not merely wrong angle. Genuinely useful here: 3 files. The builder named the fix and did not run it (15.6: cross-file the 24 rear-view Geralt frames); I checked by eye and the claim is HALF true - t0305 is a textbook three-quarter-rear, t0007 is a side profile with the face visible. Cross-filing works but needs eyes on all 24, not a bulk copy.

fresh_findings.title: A7 cannot be computed even once its images exist, because 'valid for fidelity metrics' and 'valid for art-direction metrics' are the same flag
fresh_findings.argument: pixel_metrics_valid is false for all 183 morrowind records, all 23 context, all 8 modern/ui - correct as written, since those are not used for fidelity judgements. But A7 asks for a DIFFERENT measurement over exactly those files: palette in CIELAB, luminance distribution, edge density, colour entropy, sky fraction, silhouette statistics. Two of those - edge density and colour entropy - are precisely what JPEG blocking corrupts, and 199 files carry heavily_recompressed true. Slot-level block_score medians make it concrete: REF-A4 1.50, REF-A19 1.42, REF-A2 1.42, REF-A18 1.33 - all worse than interior_darkemissive's 1.29, with bytes_per_pixel as low as 0.53. So A7's headline inter_median/intra_median would today be computed over a population where a meaningful fraction of between-region variance is JPEG artefacts, and there is no flag to filter on because the one flag that exists means something else.

fresh_findings.title: ui-combat/ is two-thirds menus, which double-counts against REF-M22 and inflates RI-UIX01
fresh_findings.argument: 8 of 12 souls-behaviour/ui-combat files are menu screens (title, options, equipment, storage x2, inventory x2, covenant); only 4 are in-combat HUD. Menus belong to REF-M22 / modern/ui. Two errors pointing opposite ways: REF-M22's real population is 16 across 4 games not 8 across 3, and RI-UIX01's is 4 not 12. Note the DS3 status screen with a live-rendered character beside the attribute column (3670478265) serves REF-M22, stance/ and R1's F7 armour-at-2m need simultaneously - good acquisition, wrong folder.

fresh_findings.title: Morrowind's UI is catalogued at rest; its defining property is that it is arranged
fresh_findings.argument: CREDIT FIRST: REF-A12b's 33 files span eight distinct resolutions from 1152x864 to 1920x1080 in both 4:3 and 16:9, which genuinely can support RI-UIX06 F18 (scaling and layout integrity) - all that is missing is a ui_resolution_pair id so the comparison is not rediscovered by eye each time. That is annotation, not acquisition. What is genuinely absent is the UI mid-use: no drag, no resize, no scrollbar part-way down a topic list, no tooltip over an inventory item, no partially-full inventory. And 15.2's claimed 8 multi-window frames have no corresponding ui_subkind in the catalogue (H9), so R1's F5 is unverifiable from the data.
fresh_findings.ruling: SUBSTITUTABLE and closing. Record the sub-kind and the resolution pairing. Do not spend a round hunting for a screenshot of a drag in progress - people do not photograph that, and keeping this BLOCKING would violate A3.

fresh_findings.title: Weather and time-of-day states, no transitions - but the set is sitting on an unexploited labelled dataset
fresh_findings.argument: Nothing in a set of independent stills can answer how a sky moves from clear to overcast or how light rotates through dusk. The unexploited asset: the Witcher 3 interval-run frames PRINT the game clock and weather in frame - I read '10:04 AM / CLEAR' off t0007 and '11:17 AM / CLEAR' off t0305. Filenames are elapsed seconds and run t0000 to t3197: 53 minutes of real time, one continuous session, ground-truth time-of-day and weather stamped in every frame. Nothing in the corpus uses it. It is enough to fit a measured time-of-day -> metric curve for one game, which is exactly the BASIS R1's F11 needed to make the overcast inference derived rather than asserted. Honest limit: all 24 are CLEAR mid-morning, so it cannot serve dusk or overcast - but it establishes the method.

fresh_findings.title: No reference for enemy placement, first-sight distance, or sightlines
fresh_findings.argument: arena/'s 14 frames answer 'what does the fighting space look like'. Not one answers 'from where, and at what distance, does the player first see the enemy' - the placement question, which decides whether a fight is readable before it starts. Every combat frame in the corpus is taken inside an engagement, because that is when people press the screenshot key.
fresh_findings.ruling: SUBSTITUTABLE, low priority. Two arena frames are already close to right; tag them and move on.

fresh_findings.title: Nothing records viewing distance, so no 'legible at combat distance' claim can be checked
fresh_findings.argument: RI-AI02's bar and RI-VIS08's creature-design seam both turn on angular size. The corpus has width, height, depicts - and no field for subject distance, subject pixel height, or fraction of frame height. REF-M6 states its own constraint in those exact terms ('40-70% of frame height') and no record carries the number, so that clause has never been checked on any file. This is R1's F9 in a new place: not a search problem, and more images will never fix it.
fresh_findings.fix: add subject_frame_fraction (coarse three-level by eye is fine) to character_closeup, souls-behaviour/telegraph, /attacks and /camera

fresh_findings.title: RI-VIS07's naming test needs 'Dark Souls' and 'Elden Ring' added, by A6's own argument
fresh_findings.argument: A6 reasoned that handing builders ESO imagery invites convergence on ESO's Black Marsh and therefore added ESO to RI-VIS07's forbidden answers. The identical argument now applies with more force: 93 Dark Souls frames were just added to a builder-facing tree. A5 rule 2's guard protects the CRITICS; it does nothing about a builder who has been looking at 91 DS3 screenshots and reaches for a gothic-cathedral silhouette, a grey-brown palette and a fog gate. Our art direction descends from Morrowind. Cheapest insurance in this document; costs nothing.

rulings.subject: builder judgement 1 (flagged reversible, 15.3): promoting the 24 Witcher 3 interval-run frames despite exif_software = 'ACDSee Ultimate 8'
rulings.ruling: UPHELD on integrity, QUALIFIED on weight
rulings.reasoning: Section 8a's exif rule is a proxy for degradation, and here degradation is directly measurable and absent: I re-measured run-w3nextgen-t0007.jpg myself at block_score 0.9868 - the lowest in the entire corpus, against a Steam median of 1.16 for the same profile; all 24 sit at 0.99-1.01. A direct measurement supersedes a proxy for it. Keep them and keep the integrity_flag verbatim - that transparency is what makes the promotion defensible. BUT the promotion carries an unpriced cost: all 24 are one location, all CLEAR mid-morning Novigrad, they are 56% of the profile they now dominate, and Novigrad is anti-generic/'s negative anchor. Apply R2C-17's weighting rule and report the band delta with and without them.

rulings.subject: builder judgement 2 (flagged reversible, 15.4): three-valued vanilla tests, null for interior REF-A12b captures
rulings.reasoning: V1 grass, V2 distant land and V4 water reflections are literally unevaluable in an interior; null with a vanilla_tests_note is more honest than unknown and is A3's reasoning applied to a test rather than a slot. Reading section 7 literally would have emptied the slot A2 calls the highest-value art-direction acquisition left. Right call, correctly flagged. ADDITION: 33 files are admitted with three of seven tests voided and nothing in their place. A menu capture has a decisive vanilla test the outdoor ones do not - the UI chrome itself, since MGE XE, OpenMW and the UI replacers all change bevel, panel colour and font visibly. Add V8 'the UI chrome matches vanilla Morrowind's bevel, panel colour and type' and score all 33. REF-A12's MyGUI data supplies checkable anchors (dialogue window 588x433, normal text RGB 202,165,96) with the caveat that OpenMW is a re-implementation, so treat them as corroboration not ground truth. Without V8, REF-A12b is the least-verified folder in the corpus and it is the one the whole UI transposition will be built from.

rulings.subject: builder judgement 3 (flagged reversible, 15.7): retaining 168 corroboration = 'one-host' records
rulings.ruling: SPLIT - upheld for the non-band axes, REVERSED for band-setting records
rulings.reasoning: Section 8b exists to stop an unverified image setting a [p10,p90] band. That risk is zero for records that can never enter a band, and souls-behaviour (93, pixel_metrics_valid false, forbidden_for fidelity-bands) and context/ (23, same) cannot. Keep them; the deviation is well reasoned and well recorded. It is NOT zero for the 36 records that are both one-host AND pixel_metrics_valid true - by definition the records that set the bands. They are: 24 W3 interval-run, 5 combat, 4 material_closeup, 2 interior_darkemissive, 1 REF-M6. In practice much less painful than it sounds: the 24 W3 frames are not Steam at all - they come from a GitHub-hosted mirror with a stated capture provenance, so 'one-host' is simply the wrong bucket; re-label, do not remove. That leaves 12 genuinely weak band-setting records: fetch each Steam detail page and read the printed date (15.5's method, already used on 95 records), or drop them from band computation while keeping them for composition. Twelve pages at one request per 4 s is under a minute.
